notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text is a full primary empirical conference report with tables and references, not an abstract or secondary article. Its title matches the neutral reference and it names Phillip Bailey, Anthony J. Onwuegbuzie, and Christine E. Daley. The title page identifies the MSERA meeting, November 17, 1999, and places Bailey first; the assigned reference is the 2000 Language Learning article with Onwuegbuzie first and DOI 10.1111/0023-8333.00112. That DOI and journal pagination are not established by this candidate. The conference version cannot independently establish the contents of journal p. 99. No PDF is supplied for layout/OCR inspection. Candidate evidence only, not assigned to any audit row: conference p. 13 reports IAS standardized beta 0.18, PAS standardized beta 0.45, and a further standardized beta 0.32 also labelled PAS in the canonical text. Do not silently relabel the latter as OAS. The three assigned descriptions mention all three scales and provide the same journal-page locator; none identifies a distinct coefficient. Conference p. 13 gives the overall regression F[3, 254]= 191.15, p < .0001, rather than a p value explicitly paired with an individual beta. Conference Table 4, p. 36, gives FLCAS correlations .64*, .77*, .73* for IAS, PAS, OAS, respectively; these are a different test and metric from the requested beta. Conference pp. 6 and 36 give 258 participants / correlation-table N; no explicit critical-regression analytic N or exclusions is established. N is not inferred from df. No arithmetic or effect-size conversion performed. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
